overview.description: Băo Huáng (literally 'Protect the Emperor') is a high-stakes, asymmetric climbing game from the Shandong province of China. Played by exactly five players with a massive 168-card deck, the game is a unique blend of card shedding and social deduction. Two 'Royals' (The Emperor and the hidden Eunuch) must clear their hands before the three 'Commoners' can stop them. The heart of the game lies in the Eunuch's hidden identity, requiring the Commoners to observe card play closely to deduce who is the traitor in their midst.

history.origins: Bao Huang emerged from the coastal cities of Shandong (specifically Qingdao and Weifang) in the mid-20th century. It traces its ancestry to simpler climbing games like 'Zheng Fen' but introduced the imperial theme and the unusually large deck to accommodate longer, more strategic social sessions.
timeline: 1960s: Developed in Shandong as a recreational game among workers.
1990s: Standardized for regional tournaments with dedicated 168-card packs.
2005: Online platforms (like QQ Games) bring Bao Huang to a national audience in China.
Present: One of the 'Big Three' Chinese climbing games alongside Zheng Fen and Sheng Ji.
history.evolution: The game's deck size has fluctuated between 168 and 216 cards across different cities, with 168 becoming the professional standard.
history.cultural: Symbolizes the complex loyalty structures of the old Chinese courts. Playing Bao Huang is often considered a 'diplomatic' skill in northern Chinese business circles.

setup.players: 5 players. Team A: Emperor & Eunuch. Team B: Three Commoners.
setup.deck: 168 cards. Take four standard 52-card decks, remove all 3s, 4s, and 5s. Use 4 Red Jokers and 4 Black Jokers. One specific Red Joker is marked 'Emperor' and one specific Black Joker is marked 'Eunuch'.
setup.dealing: Players draw cards one by one from a shuffled wall. Everyone receives 33 or 34 cards.

rules.objective: Escape the hand. Points are awarded based on the order in which players finish. The Emperor's team wins if they finish in the top positions.
rules.gameplay: Standard climbing rules: You must play the same number of cards as the leader, but of higher rank. If someone plays four 7s, you must play four 8s or higher. If you can't or won't play, you pass.
keyRules: Uprising (Zaofan): Before play, Commoners can declare an uprising if they have strong hands, doubling the stakes.
Tribute (Jin Gong): Losers of the previous round must give their highest cards to the winners at the start of the next round.
Emperor alone: If the Emperor holds both marked cards, they play against the other four alone for quadruple points.

strategy.basic: As a Commoner, never trust a 'helpful' pass. If someone passes on the Emperor's 7, they might be the Eunuch saving their high cards for later.
strategy.intermediate: The Lead Tactic: If you are the Emperor with many 6s (the lowest card), lead them in big sets (e.g., 'Six 6s') early. This forces the Commoners to break up their strong sets to stop you.
strategy.advanced: Eunuch Camouflage: The Eunuch should intentionally play a moderately high card against the Emperor early to verify their 'loyalty' to the Commoners, then switch sides at the most damaging moment.
tips: Count the Jokers. There are 8 in the deck. If 6 have been played, the last 2 are the most powerful cards in existence.
Don't waste 2s on small tricks. Save them to regain the lead when your team is ready to dump a long sequence of low cards.

list.name: Big Emperor (216 cards)
list.description: Uses four full decks including 3s, 4s, and 5s. Much longer game time.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses full 216-card deck; engine remains shared with base rules.

difficulty.easy: Reveals Eunuch identity immediately. Plays high cards on low tricks. Doesn't track played Jokers.
difficulty.medium: Logic-based deducer. Analyzes passing patterns to identify the Eunuch by the mid-game. Holds 2s for critical leads.
difficulty.hard: Perfect card counter (tracks 168 cards). Uses Bayesian inference to assign a 'Eunuch Probability' to every player. Expert at 'Tribute Management' (throwing a game to get better cards next round).

considerations: Must track identical-card frequencies (up to 4 of each rank/suit combination).
Hidden-role engine needs to handle 'Loyalty Bluffing' states.

additional: Rules of Chinese Climbing Games (Shandong Press)
The Strategy of Imperial Court Games

ante.reason: Bao Huang is a climbing game; no antes.

deal.reason: Deal is performed by dealer at start of round.

reveal_market.reason: No market; climbing game with hand only.

buy_market.reason: No buying from stock; only lead or follow.

buy_stock.reason: No stock purchase; play from hand only.

fold.reason: No folding; all players play each round.

check.reason: Use pass to skip; no check in climbing.

raise.reason: No raising; play combos or pass.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands shown when played; no reveal phase.

award_pot.reason: Scoring by points, not a pot.

play_card.description: Play a combo (single, pair, or set) to beat previous or lead.
play_card.constraints: Must follow rank and count rules; pass to skip.

draw.reason: No draw; play from hand only.

discard.reason: Cards are played to table, not discarded.

pass.description: Pass without taking another action this turn.
pass.constraints: Allowed when rules permit skipping a wager or play.

bid.reason: No bidding; Emperor and team are predetermined.

meld.reason: Climbing game; play combos, not melds.

go_out.reason: Round ends when one player empties hand.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Climbing game; play from hand only, no draw pile.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played to table, not to a discard pile.

validPlays.notes: Singles or equal-card sets; same count to beat; jokers wild.

shedding.burnRules: Same count to beat; each card must beat corresponding card; red joker unbeatable.

edgeCases.text: Commoner or emperor may declare allegiance before play; doubles score.
Losing team each gives highest non-joker to winners; emperor gives or takes two; solo emperor four; draw no tribute.
One player holds both marked jokers, plays vs four; different scoring; may declare to double.
Emperor may pass red joker left to refuse role; no exchange; continues until someone accepts.
Variant: sixes illegal until hand is only sixes; sixes cannot combine with jokers.

customActions.description: Deal 34 cards to each player from wall.
Play higher combo to beat lead.
Play Black Joker to reveal as Eunuch.
Give high cards as tribute to winner.

engine.handRankingSystem: Climbing combo order: single or equal-card sets; same count to beat; rank order Red Joker, Black Joker, 2, A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6.
engine.deckDescription: One hundred sixty-eight cards total: four standard 40-card decks (twos, threes, fours, and fives removed from each 52-card pack) combined, plus eight jokers. Four French suits in quadruplicate; red and black jokers are used as wild or special cards.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs) appear in quadruplicate (four 40-card decks). Red and black jokers are added; they may act as wild cards or have special roles in Bao Huang. Each suit has ten ranks (A, 2, 6–10, J, Q, K).
engine.rankDescription: Ten ranks per suit in each deck: ace, two, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, jack, queen, king (threes, fours, fives removed). Eight jokers (red and black) are used; their role is defined by the game rules.

hero.title: BĂO HUÁNG
hero.subtitle: Traitor in the Court
hero.tagline: 168 cards. Five players. Two Loyalists. One hidden traitor. Will the Emperor escape?

synthesis.shortDescription: Enter the high-stakes world of Shandong's premier social game. Bao Huang is a masterpiece of hidden roles and climbing strategy. As part of a 168-card marathon, you must deduce your allies, bury your low cards in massive sets, and use the power of the Eunuch to sabotage the Commoners' uprising.

prompts.human: The 168 cards are dealt. You hold 34 cards and the marked Red Joker—you are the Emperor. The Commoners are silent. Somewhere among them is your Eunuch. Lead your first set of cards and watch closely who follows.
prompts.ai: Game: Băo Huáng. Type: Climbing/Hidden-Role. Players: 5. Deck: 168 cards. Roles: Emperor/Eunuch vs 3 Commoners. Goal: Shed all cards. Feature: Eunuch is hidden until playing the special Black Joker.

scoring.description: Points are based on finishing order (1st place through 5th place).
scoring.winCondition: Calculated per hand. Typically: 1st/2nd finish by Royals = +6 points. 1st/3rd = +4 points. If Commoners take 1st, the Royals lose points.
scoring.splitRules: Emperor and Eunuch share a common pool.
